neighbours.label: the word 'contrast' and its completion (contrasted, contrast between, contraste), with irony as a weaker cousin
fire: The painting draws its power from the contrast between light and shadow.
His quiet manner contrasted sharply with his brother's loud jokes.
There was a striking contrast between the old town and the new suburbs.
The bright murals contrast with the gray concrete of the station.
Critics noted the contrast between the film's first and second halves.
The cold sea air contrasted with the warmth of the kitchen inside.
In stark contrast to her sister, she rarely spoke in public.
The novel builds on the contrast between rural and city life.
quiet: The painting draws its power from the careful use of light and shadow.
His quiet manner made him popular with the younger students.
There was a short walk from the old town to the new suburbs.
The bright murals cover the gray concrete walls of the station.
Critics praised the music in the film's first and second halves.
The cold sea air came in through the open kitchen window.
Like her sister, she rarely spoke in public about her work.
The novel builds a detailed picture of rural and city life.
